migration_and_data_impact: None. Guard, test and record changes only; no schema, migration, provider, credential or customer-data effect.
compatibility_impact: No contract-catalog file changes. A test file, or a .mjs module in a test's import closure, that imports from outside the repository, through a symbolic link, an undigested file, a non-literal import(), a plainly spelled require/createRequire, a \u escape, CR, U+2028 or U+2029 now fails the guard with exit 92; none exists at this head (guard exit 0).
known_limitations: The test-integrity guard is a tripwire, not a control: a commit that edits a guarded file and its digest together passes (open_blockers[1]).

The E4 import walk reads code through stripNonCode, a scanner and not a parser. Known misreads that can hide an import, recorded OPEN in open_blockers[11] and not claimed exhaustive: an import after a nested template inside ${...}; after a regex literal that follows ')' or 'of'; after a division that follows '++', '--' or '}'. Each needs a digested file edited and its digest regenerated, so each is in the digest class of open_blockers[1].

Runtime loaders are not walked: new Function, direct and indirect eval, node:vm, Worker, module.register and computed members; nor a spawned process or files read as data. These too need a digested file edited.
The declared/executed reconciliation (exit 88) compares counts, not identities, and there is a parse/hash/load race (open_blockers[10]).
open_risks_or_blockers: Tripwire: a commit that edits a guarded file and its digest together passes; the anchor is outside the repository (manifest open_blockers[1]).
